# Uber: dated valuation research, v2

Information cutoff: **19 October 2026**. Operating/capital anchor: **30 June 2026**. Currency: USD; monetary tables are millions unless stated. This is a primary-source research package and a conditional model, not a current trading target. No canonical company record, application, repository commit or publication is changed.

## Decision-useful result

Uber is a large NYSE-listed mobility, delivery and freight platform, suitable for a broader consumer/services research universe. It is not an AI-infrastructure vendor. That classification does **not** mean it has no AI exposure: autonomous-vehicle partnerships can change platform bargaining power, take rates, investment requirements and competition. Its issuer announced conditional Rivian investment of up to $1.25bn through 2031, with vehicle purchases potentially undertaken by Uber or fleet partners. The model does not assume those vehicles are costless. [Issuer announcement](https://investor.uber.com/news-events/news/press-release-details/2026/Uber-and-Rivian-Partner-to-Deploy-up-to-50000-Fully-Autonomous-Robotaxis-2026-TViR4R05gi/)

| Analyst scenario | Operating EV, $bn | Terminal share of EV | Conditional June allocation, $/share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Bear | 62.95 | 46.80% | 29.15 |
| Base | 190.60 | 59.05% | 90.75 |
| Bull | 422.73 | 69.94% | 202.77 |

The final column requires the separately labeled illustration policy. It is not the default, a verified historical fair value, a probability-weighted expectation or an October price target. It uses a June share count reported to the nearest thousand and explicitly assumed existing-award, investment, tax, lease and minority-claim values. The unselected policy correctly returns null per-share values. The wide range reflects real uncertainty rather than a price-matching exercise; no share price or analyst price target is an input.

## Reported operating evidence

The 2025 annual report shows revenue of $52.017bn, operating income of $5.565bn, adjusted EBITDA of $8.730bn, CFO of $10.099bn and cash PP&E purchases of $336m. H1 2026 revenue/operating income were $27.394bn/$3.813bn; H1 2025 were $24.184bn/$2.678bn. Thus the June TTM revenue and GAAP EBIT anchors are $55.227bn and $6.700bn. This arithmetic and the cited statement locations are retained in `latest-financials-v2.json`. [2025 SEC annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1543151/000154315126000015/uber-20251231.htm), [June SEC quarterly report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1543151/000154315126000032/uber-20260630.htm)

TTM gross bookings are $215.622bn: Mobility $107.935bn, Delivery $102.208bn and Freight $5.479bn. Bookings are a platform-volume measure. They include taxes/tolls/fees and precede participant earnings and consumer adjustments; driver tips are excluded. Revenue is generally net when Uber acts as agent and gross where it is principal. A reported revenue/bookings ratio is therefore **not a uniform contractual take rate**. Advertising, merchant/driver incentives and geographic/product mix also matter. See the quarterly bookings and segment revenue evidence in `operating-mix-history-v2.json`.

The January 2, 2026 UK change is particularly important: driver payments moved from cost of revenue to contra-revenue in affected markets, reducing H1 reported revenue by about $2.1bn and Q2 by about $1.1bn. A declining revenue ratio need not mean deteriorating fee economics. We forecast bookings and revenue presentation ratios separately and anchor GAAP operating profitability to bookings.

Q2 2026 GAAP operating income was $1.890bn, non-GAAP operating income $2.143bn and adjusted EBITDA $2.819bn. Those are distinct. H1 2026 segment figures in the quarterly filing use Segment Operating Income, while the 2025 annual report uses Segment Adjusted EBITDA. The new report recasts its prior-year quarter comparatives, not every historical segment year in this package. Never splice the measures as a continuous margin series. [Issuer earnings reconciliation filed with SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1543151/000154315126000027/uberq226earningspressrelea.htm)

## Historical scope: ten slots, not ten identical businesses

`history-v2.json/csv` contains 2016–2025. Nine years have the major annual cash-flow fields; 2016 is partial selected history, with missing CFO/capex preserved as null. The 2020 annual report supplies unaudited selected 2016–2017 columns. Its 2016 figures are retrospectively ASC606-recast; pre-2019 leases are not ASC842-recast.

A material extraction trap was repaired: SEC companyfacts retained older 2017 revenue of $7.932bn, but the 2020 selected-data recast is $7.402bn. The 2020 policy moved excess cumulative driver payments out of cost of revenue and into revenue reductions. Recast 2018/2019 revenues are $10.433bn/$13.000bn rather than $11.270bn/$14.147bn; operating income and cash flow did not change. `history-comparability-v2.json` keeps the reconciliation. [2020 SEC annual report, Item 6 and Note 1](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1543151/000154315121000014/uber-20201231.htm)

Other boundaries include China/Southeast Asia/Russia disposals, the 2019 IPO and large vesting charge, the pandemic, Careem/Postmates/Transplace and other acquisitions, Careem Technologies deconsolidation, the 2022 UK principal-model change, and the 2026 reversal. Pre-IPO preferred equity and historical weighted-average share counts cannot serve as today's ownership denominator. The package does not claim constant-perimeter organic comparability. Every nonmissing extracted field has a source/tag or direct-table provenance entry; a complete manual audit of every historical tag is still pending.

## Cash quality and claim treatment

- **Insurance:** June reserves total $13.286bn. Restricted cash plus restricted investments total $11.793bn. These are operating funding stocks; the pool is not free cash. The pool-to-reserve mapping is an analyst proxy because the disclosure does not establish that every restricted dollar solely backs these exact reserves. Reported 2025 CFO included a $2.660bn reserve increase. The forecast explicitly adds reserve growth and subtracts collateral growth rather than capitalizing the entire CFO benefit as freely distributable cash. Base collateral reaches 100% of reserve, causing a $1.493bn first-year catch-up. There is no second reserve deduction or restricted-asset credit in the equity bridge. Recovery receivables and interest earned on the restricted portfolio are not separately valued, a conservative limitation. Ultimate insurance severity and timing remain uncertain.
- **SBC:** Recurring labor expense remains inside modeled GAAP EBIT. There is no SBC addback and no second future dilution schedule for the same labor. Existing earned equity rights require a separate allocation. The illustrative 32.321m incremental units are a deliberate assumption, not the gross 71.804m unvested award count, EPS dilution or an audited earned-award count. Options get a separate assumed $200m claim, compared with disclosed aggregate intrinsic value of $132m; this is not a Black–Scholes appraisal. Future-service overlap still needs independent review.
- **D&A/reinvestment:** Operating D&A differs from CFO D&A: 2025 is $719m versus $747m, and H1 2026 is $372m versus $386m. Only operating D&A is added in FCFF. Gross asset reinvestment of 1.5–2.0% of revenue is an explicit budget above recent cash PP&E purchases, including assumed future finance-leased asset funding. R&D remains expensed; acquired-company earnings are not introduced without their investment costs.
- **Taxes:** 2024/2025 GAAP tax benefits include valuation-allowance releases; they are not recurring cash inflows. Cash taxes paid were $345m in 2025 and $280m in H1 2026. Forecast rates are normalized at 27%/25%/23% from year one through terminal. The $10.162bn June deferred tax asset is not added to equity. This deliberately omits some tax-asset optionality rather than counting it twice.
- **Investments:** Listed equity, nonmarketable positions, equity-method stakes, Delivery Hero total-return swaps and loans have different realization risks. `investment-detail-v2.json` records the June categories. The illustration applies disclosed-category valuation haircuts; it is not a current mark-to-market. Other derivative assets of $147m, including $136m embedded derivatives disclosed in June Note 2, are not separately credited; this is an additional conservative omission, not unrestricted cash. Aurora's pledged shares and exchangeable notes are paired through the total-debt claim, with no second penalty merely for pledging the same asset.
- **Debt and leases:** June debt carrying value is $12.723bn; the disclosed approximate fair value is $12.9bn. The illustration uses fair value once, thereby including the convertible option and exchangeable-note economics instead of also adding conversion shares. Operating lease rent stays in EBIT and its $2.008bn balance is not again deducted. June finance-lease principal is not separately disclosed in the retrieved Q; the illustration's $140m equals December $222m less H1 principal payments $82m under an explicit no-additions/FX assumption. This is a provisional estimate, not a reported June balance.
- **Other claims:** Consolidated FCFF requires allocation to NCI. The illustration uses $903m nonredeemable and $180m redeemable book proxies; it also reserves $1.841bn legal/regulatory/nonincome-tax and $1.042bn income/other-tax balances, plus explicit mixed-claim and prospective investment/vehicle allowances. Those choices are not estimates of ultimate litigation outcomes. UK disputed VAT amounts already paid are not counted as available cash or an assured refund. No unknown is silently set to zero.

## Why these operating assumptions?

The TTM GAAP EBIT/bookings margin is about 3.11%; H1 2026 is about 3.41%. Base starts at 3.5% and reaches 5.2% over ten years: continued scale benefits and delivery improvement, with meaningful insurance, support, marketing, R&D and SBC still paid. Bear settles at 3.2%, representing pricing/regulatory/insurance pressure. Bull reaches 6.5%, which requires sustained platform leverage and stronger economics; it should not be treated as a trend-line entitlement.

Base Mobility/Delivery bookings growth fades from 15%/18% to 5%/5.5%; bear starts at 10%/12%, bull at 18%/22%. These are deliberately below or around recent growth at the outset and fade substantially. They exclude automatic Delivery Hero/ezCater consolidation. Forecast revenue presentation ratios approximate the post-UK-change mix, rather than repeating the distorted old Mobility ratio.

WACC is 11.5%/9.5%/8.0%, perpetual growth 2%/2.5%/3%, and terminal ROIC 18%/25%/30%. These are **analyst hurdle-rate/scenario choices**, not a claimed contemporaneous CAPM estimate, observed beta, Treasury quote or management guidance. They bracket uncertain regulation, competitive durability, financing and capital needs. All are editable. A 25-cell WACC/g sensitivity grid recalculates terminal reinvestment. The terminal FCFF deducts at least NOPAT × growth / ROIC, preventing perpetually growing EBIT from requiring no incremental capital.

## The June-to-October bridge is material

The June balance sheet is not the October capitalization. Events are sourced individually in `post-june-capital-events-v2.json`:

1. Getir closed July 1 for approximately $465m cash covering 100% of the food business plus a minority grocery interest. The bridge separates acquired food operating EV from the grocery investment asset; consideration is not automatically operating EV. Careem Technologies became controlled July 30. Its earlier investment is removed at the selected June allocation value ($117.6m in the illustration, versus $147m reported book); consideration, acquired cash, debt, NCI and other claims remain explicit separate inputs.
2. Blacklane's own August 20 partner notice says it was officially acquired. The earlier SEC agreement disclosed about $550m, but the exact closing date and actual cash need confirmation; the current bridge requires an explicit assumption. [Acquiree notice](https://partner-help.blacklane.com/en/articles/14324796-uber-to-acquire-global-chauffeur-service-blacklane)
3. August financing included €4bn of acquisition term commitments, reducing the original €14.2bn bridge commitment, and a $7.7bn replacement revolver. Commitments are not cash or outstanding debt; the new revolver was undrawn at closing. [SEC August 7 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1543151/000155278126000414/e26328_uber-8k.htm)
4. September 15 notes issued have €4,500m principal. Public issue prices produce €4,489.3075m gross proceeds, a €10.6925m issue discount. Underwriting discounts of €24.875m leave €4,464.4325m before other expenses. The final prospectus estimates net proceeds of approximately €4,453m, implying roughly €11.4325m other expenses; that is an estimate, not an exact realized cash confirmation. Annual coupons total €200m. Both known discounts are fixed in the engine; only other expenses require an explicit choice. [Pricing term sheet](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1543151/000155278126000479/e26381_uber-fwp.htm), [underwriting agreement Schedule I](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1543151/000155278126000486/e26383_ex1-1.htm), [final prospectus front table and S-13](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1543151/000155278126000481/e26382_uber-euro424b2.htm)
5. Delivery Hero's €41.50/share offer remained conditional, with acceptance through November 5 and settlement expected H2 2027. ezCater's $2.3bn all-cash agreement was announced October 6 and remained pending. Neither is automatically consolidated, paid for or financed in the June core. [Delivery Hero offer status](https://investor.uber.com/news-events/news/press-release-details/2026/Uber-Publishes-Offer-Document-for-its-Takeover-Offer-for-Delivery-Hero/default.aspx), [ezCater agreement](https://investor.uber.com/news-events/news/press-release-details/2026/Uber-to-Acquire-ezCater-as-it-Brings-Catering-to-Uber-Eats/default.aspx)

The optional rollforward engine can produce a conditional October allocation once every missing cash, claim, share and investment assumption is supplied. It rolls June EV by elapsed WACC and removes **economic** interim FCFF at a midpoint convention. Actual operating cash is separately reconciled for the economic cash-replacement SBC convention, cash taxes, collateral/working capital, reinvestment timing and other operating differences. Actual interest paid is then deducted in full once. Signed nonoperating receipts/payments handle investment sales, option/ESPP proceeds and other items without incorrectly reducing operating EV. Pair investment dispositions with asset removal and equity issuance with the ownership ledger.

Retained euro-note cash and the notes are both translated at current FX. Cash converted or spent at other dates requires an explicit disposition and realized-FX reconciliation; other currency cash translation is separate. Each closed deal has named cash, operating EV, debt, NCI and other-claim entries, with Getir grocery value separate. Every current inherited lease, NCI, option, tax/legal and other claim must be expressly selected; leaving a June value unchanged is a stated assumption. The price fraction for new debt represents its entire current claim, including accrued interest. Current exact shares are unknown; July 31's exact 2,042,560,121 is an observation at that date only, and the model requires whole shares.

The June $2bn term loan matures in December 2026. Its remaining $1bn commitment could only be drawn through August 2; it is not automatically available in October. The existing loan is already in the June debt deduction, so maturity is a funding issue, not another debt claim to subtract. Neither the equity allocation nor the aggregate ending-cash guard certifies daily/future liquidity. [June report, Note 5](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1543151/000154315126000032/uber-20260630.htm)

`OCTOBER-BRIDGE-v2.md` explains the exact ledger and sign conventions. Complete numerical fixtures in the verifier are deliberately synthetic arithmetic tests, not current operating forecasts or recommended valuation policies.

## Readiness

Author checks are recorded in `verification-v2.json`. They cover source/date rules, the recast-history repair, balance-sheet and profit bridges, 30 annual FCFF rows, terminal reinvestment, dated allocation, invalid inputs, and paired financing/closed-deal arithmetic. These do not independently validate economic assumptions or certify complete claims/funding. The independent v1 review reconstructed June EV and the illustrative allocation without finding a numerical error, and requested corrections to the optional October bridge. This v2 implements those corrections; independent v2 review, claim resolution and a verified October capitalization remain required before current-equity admission. Model/research review is ready; publication/admission is not authorized or performed.
